title: Why Electrification Could Cut Global Energy Use in Half!
summary:
Why Electrification Could Cut Global Energy Use in Half!
In this episode of the Everything Electric PODCAST, Robert Llewellyn sits down with Professor Jan Rosenow, Professor of Energy and Climate Policy at Oxford University, to reveal why electricity currently only tells 20% of the global energy story.
Jan explains how shifting to electrification at scale could cut total global energy demand in half and tackles the biggest myths and milestones of the transition:The Grid Threat: Why data centers pose a more significant regional challenge to the grid than 100 million electric vehicles.
A look at the “mind-blowing” scale of solar adoption in China and the declining utilization of their coal plants.
Beyond Climate: Why electrification is now a primary lever for energy security and economic resilience in a volatile world.

title: Bute House protested by environmental campaigners
summary:
Environmental campaigners have staged a Halloween themed demonstration outside the first minister's official residence over "scary" fossil fuels.
Climate groups gathered outside Bute House in Edinburgh to protest against the Scottish government's decision to give the go-ahead for a new, gas-fired, power station at Peterhead in Aberdeenshire.
The decision has been branded a "catastrophic failure" by environmental campaigners, who said burning fossil fuels is the key driver of extreme weather such as recent storms, record heat and flooding.
The protest also comes after the announcement from the UK government that the Jackdaw gas field near Aberdeen would be allowed to go ahead.
Protesters wearing Halloween themed masks and holding placards with messages such as "fossil fuel ghouls" and "this decision will haunt you" gathered on Charlotte Square.

title: UK weather: 10 days without rain after 'wettest week in two years'
summary:
The UK could see as many as 10 consecutive days without rain after an unsettled end to October that featured back-to-back storms.
It comes after the Environment Agency said England experienced its wettest week in two years thanks to Storms Austen and Boelo.
Following this recent unsettled weather, the return of high pressure will bring a prolonged spell of largely dry and calm conditions, with very little rain in sight.
Mist and fog will remain a persistent feature, with some slow-clearing dense patches expected during the mornings.

title: There are significant amounts of microplastic in Sierra Nevada snow
summary:
University University of California, RiversideFor the first time, scientists have measured how much microplastic pollution falls on the Sierra Nevada during snowstorms and were surprised to find significant amounts even in the most remote locations.
As snowflakes fall, they collect some of these tiny plastic particles suspended in the air.
This process, called scavenging, helps explain why researchers measured substantially more plastic arriving with the falling snow than during dry weather.
At remote sampling locations, during the height of the storm, the snow deposited between 270 and 3,200 plastic particles per square meter, per day.
Researchers used infrared light to read chemical signatures, then compared those signatures with a reference library to distinguish plastic from soil and plant material.

title: Global nature talks reach deal but money remains an issue
summary:
The world's nations have been gathered in Yerevan for nearly two weeks negotiating, and arguing, over a new agreement on nature.
Early on Saturday morning, hours after talks were due to finish, they finally agreed the key parts of a new action plan.
Four years earlier the same countries had signed a landmark deal committing to "halt and reverse" the decline of nature.
That global deal in 2022 - the Global Biodiversity Framework - contained 24 targets including putting 30% of the world's land and seas into protection by the end of the decade.
As part of this week's deal, countries acknowledged they were falling behind.

title: The EPA is quietly killing its web archive
summary:
In a little-noticed webpage update, the Environmental Protection Agency has announced a plan to decommission its online web archive at the end of the year, a move that would wipe tens of thousands of publicly available environmental resources from the web.
“This information is irreplaceable, and if the archive is decommissioned, that information will be lost forever.”For decades, the web archive has been an unparalleled resource for researchers, legislators, policymakers, and the public writ large.
Screenshot of the EPA’s online archive webpage Rachel SantarsieroThis isn’t the first time the environmental agency has tried to shutter the online web archive.
Here's HowAfter five months of public backlash, the EPA acquiesced, in part by announcing it would delay the web archive’s retirement by one year to July 2023.
“EPA should expand and systematize the archive, not throw it away and expect that three discrete snapshots will suffice,” said Gehrke.

title: Broughshane Waterfowl Park: Recovery effort continues after oil tank vandalism
summary:
Recovery efforts are continuing after an oil spill caused by the vandalism of a nearby home heating oil tank resulted in the death of 13 birds from Broughshane Waterfowl Park.
More than 20 birds were transported to the USPCA's headquarters last week for urgent specialist care, but the death toll has continued to rise.
The popular attraction in County Antrim has been forced to close while efforts continue to remove oil from the pond.
Police have appealed for anyone with information to come forward.
